_comment: 16-target Vulhub shortlist from funnypot/docs/research/dataset-indexes-and-vulhub.md section 3.1, plus 2 honorable-mention extras from the same doc (included: false). vulhub_dir/image/host_port/banner_path/cve_trigger were verified against github.com/vulhub/vulhub@master docker-compose.yml + README.md on 2026-08-19 -- re-verify before a real run, vulhub updates image tags over time. license_flag follows section 3.6: 'internal_only' targets bake a proprietary/repackaged binary into the published Docker Hub image (Oracle/Atlassian/GitLab) -- captures from those must never leave this project's own infra, per the README.

license_flag_meanings.oss: Software running in the container is OSS (permissive or copyleft). Internal training is low-risk; still don't republish vendor-branded static assets (logos/CSS) verbatim if the corpus is ever shared externally.
license_flag_meanings.internal_only: The image itself bakes in a proprietary/repackaged binary (Oracle WebLogic, Atlassian Confluence, GitLab EE). Captures are internal-training-only -- never redistribute the corpus, never publish an example body from these targets, even in a blog post.

targets.name: httpd-cve-2021-41773
targets.image: build:. (Apache httpd 2.4.49, built from the target's own Dockerfile -- no pinned registry tag)
targets.notes: Path-traversal GET, no exploit payload needed for a real version banner.

targets.name: httpd-cve-2021-42013
targets.image: build:. (Apache httpd 2.4.50, built from the target's own Dockerfile -- no pinned registry tag)
targets.notes: Same family as #1, patched-then-rebroken -- second real Apache version banner.

targets.name: php-cve-2019-11043
targets.notes: nginx+PHP-FPM: real nginx headers fronting real PHP errors -- funnypot's own likely stack.

targets.name: thinkphp-5.0.23-rce
targets.notes: High real-world scan volume (Chinese botnet staple); distinctive X-Powered-By + framework error page.

targets.name: struts2-s2-045

cve_trigger.note: OGNL injection rides the Content-Type header, not the path -- trigger is header-based; see the target README before automating it

targets.notes: The Equifax CVE. cve_trigger needs a crafted Content-Type header, so it's excluded from the default replay list -- fire it manually if wanted.

targets.name: spring-cve-2022-22965

cve_trigger.note: Multi-request PoC (class-loader gadget then a dropped webshell) -- see target README, not a single safe replay line

targets.notes: Massive 2022 scan wave; real Spring Boot Whitelabel error page on unknown paths.

targets.name: spring-cve-2022-22947
targets.notes: Different Spring stack persona (Actuator/Gateway banners) from #6.

targets.name: log4j-cve-2021-44228
targets.notes: The single highest-volume scanned CVE ever. cve_trigger is safe to fire on the internal-only network -- it's an outbound LDAP lookup, not a payload; the docker network's egress block just makes it fail closed.

targets.name: weblogic-cve-2020-14882
targets.notes: Oracle binaries baked into vulhub's published image -- internal-training-only, see license_flag_meanings.

targets.name: drupal-cve-2018-7600
targets.notes: Real Drupal error/maintenance pages; GPL CMS persona.

targets.name: gitlab-cve-2021-22205

cve_trigger.note: ExifTool RCE via an avatar upload (multi-request poc.py flow, not a single GET/POST line) -- see target README

targets.notes: Slowest target to boot (Rails + Postgres + Redis) -- give the health check a long timeout. Treated internal_only per the design doc even though GitLab CE is itself open-source, because vulhub bakes a specific EE-era image under its own account (section 3.6).

targets.name: confluence-cve-2022-26134
targets.notes: Needs a Confluence trial license key to get past setup before most paths resolve -- see target README. Atlassian binaries baked into vulhub's image -- internal-training-only.

targets.name: jenkins-cve-2024-23897

cve_trigger.note: Fired via jenkins-cli.jar over its own CLI-over-HTTP channel, not a plain curl-able path -- proxying it needs -Dhttp.proxyHost/-Dhttp.proxyPort on the java invocation; not wired into the default driver

targets.notes: Recent + still relevant; real Jenkins banner/login chrome. cve_trigger left manual -- see notes above.

targets.name: tomcat-cve-2020-1938

cve_trigger.note: Ghostcat is an AJP-protocol (port 8009) exploit, not HTTP -- out of scope for this HTTP-only recorder, per the design doc's protocol-scope note

targets.notes: /manager/html is one of the most-probed paths on the internet; capture is HTTP-only (port 8080), the AJP CVE itself is not recordable through mitmdump's HTTP proxy.

targets.name: solr-cve-2019-17558

cve_trigger.note: Two-step PoC (enable velocity via this POST, then a crafted GET to /solr/demo/select) -- see target README

targets.notes: /solr/admin/ probes are constant background scanner noise; distinctive Solr admin JSON/HTML shape.

targets.name: phpmyadmin-cve-2018-12613
targets.notes: Near-universal scanner target; matches the stock phpMyAdmin container LLM-TRAINING-DATA.md already plans.

targets.name: shiro-cve-2016-4437

cve_trigger.note: Trigger is a crafted `Cookie: rememberMe=<encrypted_payload>` header, not a path -- see target README

targets.notes: Design-doc honorable mention #17 (Shiro-550). Extremely common in scan logs via its distinctive Cookie header; add if time allows -- not built into the default 16-target run.

targets.name: fastjson-1.2.47-rce

cve_trigger.note: Needs an attacker-controlled RMI/LDAP callback server outside the sandbox -- do not attempt inside the no-egress network; banner-only capture is still fine

targets.notes: Design-doc honorable mention #18. Near-ubiquitous in JSON-API probe traffic; add if time allows -- not built into the default 16-target run.
